name: Powered Micromobility Device
description: From January 1, 2027, a powered vehicle designed to carry a person, under 100 pounds unloaded, with a top speed of 28 mph, that isn't an electric assisted bicycle, motor assisted scooter, moped or motorcycle. Mopeds and motorcycles have seats, so a standing electric scooter past a motor assisted scooter's 20 mph or 1,000 watts lands here, and is treated as a bicycle.

restrictions.rule: Designed to transport a person, with a propulsion system, a maximum speed of 28 mph and an unloaded weight under 100 pounds; no limit on motor power
Excludes electric assisted bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, motor assisted scooters, motorized wheelchairs, motorcycles, mopeds and all-terrain vehicles
Not a motor vehicle: its rider has the rights and duties of a bicycle rider, and it needs no title, registration or insurance
Riders must be 16 or older, and need no driver's license
restrictions.citation: Oregon Revised Statutes §807.020, as amended by HB 4007 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders and passengers under 16 must wear an approved bicycle-type helmet; a parent, or a rider carrying such a passenger, is liable for the violation
restrictions.citation: Oregon Revised Statutes §814.486, as amended by HB 4007 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Allowed in bicycle lanes and on bicycle paths, though a local government or state agency may ban or regulate it on bicycle lanes, paths, sidewalks and trails
restrictions.citation: Oregon Revised Statutes §811.440, as amended by HB 4007 (2026); HB 4007 (2026) §4

restrictions.rule: Selling one as a powered micromobility device when it doesn't fit the definition, or is built or meant to be taken out of it by a switch, a change to its motor or drive system, or an app, is a Class D traffic violation and an unlawful trade practice
A new one, or its battery or charger, may only be sold with a certification mark from an accredited testing laboratory
